judge.reason: The answer plainly rejects the 98% readiness/confidence claim. It calls for a fresh held-out representative set, executable output and side-effect state checks, and a separate blinded, order-randomized judge calibrated against human labels for subjective quality. It also requires counting timeouts and aborted runs as failures, versioning the full configuration, per-slice results, and a ~89–99.9% interval, while distinguishing accuracy from statistical confidence and reruns from independent samples; it honestly says nothing was run (only a Skill load is shown), and its one gap is not explicitly requiring causes for each failure.
